1#א: Its law is like [that of] a beriah. As stated [above]: 'and likewise etc.' and 'it is necessary etc.' — as discussed above (in siman 100, se'if katan 5).
1#ב: That even etc. — As noted above from the Tosefta and the Gemara at the beginning of chapter 8 of Zevachim, and chapter 1 of [tractate] Yom Tov (Beitzah), and chapter 5 of Avodah Zarah (daf 74a): 'and these are forbidden etc.' And [the Gemara] challenges there: 'let it also teach [the case of] a piece of neveilah etc.' — see Tosafot there, s.v. 'l'me'utei etc.' And for this reason it appears [the word] comes to exclude etc. And likewise the Bach there [holds this is so] because it is a piece worthy of honor (chaticha ha'ra'uya l'hitchabed), which is a thing [prohibited by rabbinic] count (davar shebeminyan). See Tosafot there, s.v. 'ha etc.,' and in Chullin 100a, s.v. 'sha'ani etc.,' and one can explain that this is its meaning etc.
1#ג: And even if it is etc. — See the aforementioned Tosafot in Avodah Zarah, s.v. 'ha,' and in Chullin there, s.v. 'sha'ani etc.'
1#ד: Since if etc. and it is worthy of honor. That is to say, to exclude pieces of a sin-offering [discussed] in the chapter ha'Areil — for even if they were to become nullified, they remain forbidden to non-priests, and to priests they are not worthy of honor. See the aforementioned Tosafot in Chullin, s.v. [above], and in Yevamot, chapter 1, daf 20, s.v. 'divrei etc.'
1#ה: And even if it is not etc. — As is written regarding yayin nesech in Avodah Zarah. See the aforementioned Tosafot, s.v. 'ha etc.,' and [their question]: 'and if so, yayin nesech etc.' And in Yevamot, chapter 1, daf 1, s.v. 'mai etc.'
1#ו: And if it is doubtful etc. — As will be discussed in siman 110, seif 1, in the Rama's gloss, [the rule] that something of importance etc.; and as written in Gittin 54b — see Rashi there, s.v. 'lo ya'alu,' and Tosafot in Zevachim 73b, s.v. 'ela etc.'
2#א: It has no [nullification] etc. — From what is taught in the Mishnah in Chullin 96b: 'and likewise a piece etc., and likewise a piece etc.' — those specific [cases] alone are enumerated precisely. [Collection:] It has no [nullification] etc. — For it is not superior to a species mixed with its own species according to Rav Yehuda, where it is not nullified d'oraisa, and yet even so in such a case it is nullified — except in basar b'chalav. See Tosafot, Chullin 108b, s.v. 'amai etc.' (end of quote).
2#ב: Such as neveilah — in the chapter Gid HaNasheh and there.
3#א: A chicken etc., and likewise etc., and likewise etc. — From the fact that [the Gemara] in Zevachim there challenges: 'let them be nullified by a majority!' — even though there are many pieces worthy of honor (chatichot ha're'uyot l'hitchabed) among them — since as it is [in its whole, intact state] it is not [considered] worthy of honor. And likewise in the Yerushalmi, which Tosafot cite in Yevamot there, [the Gemara] interprets the Mishnah of Avodah Zarah as referring to a slaughtered ox [and the Rash in chapter 3 of Orlah wrote in the name of the Yerushalmi: in a cut piece]. And even though in our Gemara in Zevachim there it appears to refer to a living animal, nevertheless it states there that it is specifically because it is a living creature (ba'al chayim) that it is not nullified.
3#ב: And even though etc. — As noted in siman 99, seif 6, that in such a case [the forbidden status] does not revive [once nullified]. See there.
3#ג: And some disagree with all of this — see Tosafot in Zevachim 72a, s.v. 'ela etc.,' and in Yevamot chapter 1, daf 2, [where] Rabbi Yochanan etc. And the proof is from the fact that [the Talmud] counts among the six things: beets, cabbage, and gourd — and these are not normally cooked whole, hence it must be referring to them when alive. And likewise in Avodah Zarah, which counts the birds of the metzora etc. — [this is the view of] the Rosh. And according to this, even a chicken in its feathers is like the birds of the metzora.
3#ד: And so the practice is, except for etc., and likewise etc. — [This follows] the first position, except that one can say that the ox condemned to stoning is different, since it lacks a major rectification [before it could ever become permitted].
3#ה: And likewise fish etc. — See Bava Batra, chapter 3, [daf] 2, in the Mishnah.
5#_: The gizzard and likewise etc. — As written in [tractate] Yom Tov (Beitzah) 7a, and Nedarim 54b, and Meilah 20b.
6#א: This etc. — Beriah was explained in the preceding siman; and piece worthy of honor (chaticha ha'ra'uya l'hitchabed) is as stated in the aforementioned Tosefta: 'a forbidden piece that became mixed among [other] pieces — even if they number a thousand, they are all forbidden' — and the gravy [is assessed] by noten taam (imparting flavor). If it dissolved, it [is assessed] by noten taam. And in Yevamot chapter 1, daf 2, [the case of] when it dissolved. See Tosafot there, s.v. 'divrei etc.,' and in the Mishnah, chapter 2 of Orlah: 'how [is it if] they were crushed etc.'
6#ב: Until it is lost etc. — This applies only to piece worthy of honor (chaticha ha'ra'uya l'hitchabed), as stated in the preceding siman.
6#ג: And even if etc. — Gittin 54b: 'they fell [and were] crushed etc.' See Rashi there, s.v. 'naflu etc.'
6#ד: And even after etc. — From the fact that it states there [the rule concerning one who acted] deliberately etc. And as noted in siman 99, seif 5, in the Rama's gloss. See there.
6#ה: And that is when they were crushed etc. — Gittin there.
6#ו: To crush etc., and likewise etc. — As noted in siman 99, seif 5. See there.
6#ז: And there is no distinction etc. — The location of this Rama's gloss is at the beginning of this siman. That is to say, a piece worthy of honor (chaticha ha'ra'uya l'hitchabed) is not nullified even among things not of its own species (she'eino mino), contrary to the Or Zarua, who compares beriah and piece worthy of honor to something that has a permitted aspect (davar she'yesh lo matirin). See above, siman 100, seif 3 and seif 4. And as written in the chapter 'Elu Trefot' (daf 67a): 'a person should not skin etc.' And even though presumably there is more than sixty times [the permitted material] relative to it — (according to Rashi there this is not a proof — see the end of siman 100). And see what is written at the beginning of siman 110. See there.
7#_: If it was cut etc., and even etc. — Zevachim 74b.
8#_: The gizzard etc., the head etc. — Avodah Zarah 40a.
